sa: तेषां निष्ठा तु का कृष्ण सत्त्वमाहो रजस्तमः ॥
tr: teṣāṃ niṣṭhā tu kā kṛṣṇa sattvamāho rajastamaḥ
en: Those who set aside the rules of scripture yet worship with faith, Krishna: what is their standing? Is it goodness, passion or dullness?
speaker: Arjuna said

sa: त्रिविधा भवति श्रद्धा देहिनां सा स्वभावजा।
सात्त्विकी राजसी चैव तामसी चेति तां श्रृणु ॥
tr: trividhā bhavati śraddhā dehināṃ sā svabhāvajā
sāttvikī rājasī caiva tāmasī ceti tāṃ śrṛṇu
en: The faith of embodied beings is of three kinds, born of their own nature: of goodness, of passion and of dullness. Hear about it.
speaker: Krishna said

sa: श्रद्धामयोऽयं पुरुषो यो यच्छ्रद्धः स एव सः ॥
tr: śraddhāmayo'yaṃ puruṣo yo yacchraddhaḥ sa eva saḥ
en: Everyone's faith takes the shape of their inner being, Bharata. A person is made of their faith; as their faith is, so are they.
People of goodness worship the gods; people of passion worship yakshas and rakshasas; and others, of dullness, worship ghosts and spirits.

sa: अशास्त्रविहितं घोरं तप्यन्ते ये तपो जनाः।
tr: aśāstravihitaṃ ghoraṃ tapyante ye tapo janāḥ
en: Those who practise terrible austerities not taught by scripture, given to hypocrisy and ego, driven by desire, attachment and force,
senseless, tormenting the elements in the body and me who dwell within the body: know them to be of demonic resolve.
Even the food that each person likes is of three kinds, and so are sacrifice, austerity and giving. Hear how they differ.

sa: रस्याः स्निग्धाः स्थिरा हृद्या आहाराः सात्त्विकप्रियाः ॥
tr: rasyāḥ snigdhāḥ sthirā hṛdyā āhārāḥ sāttvikapriyāḥ
en: Foods that increase life, vitality, strength, health, happiness and cheer, that are savoury, smooth, nourishing and pleasing to the heart, are dear to people of goodness.
Foods that are bitter, sour, salty, too hot, pungent, dry and burning, bringing pain, grief and sickness, are liked by people of passion.

sa: यातयामं गतरसं पूति पर्युषितं च यत्।
tr: yātayāmaṃ gatarasaṃ pūti paryuṣitaṃ ca yat
en: Food that is stale, tasteless, putrid, spoiled, left over and impure is dear to people of dullness.
The sacrifice offered as scripture directs by those who seek no reward, with the mind fixed on the thought "this ought to be done," is of goodness.

sa: अभिसंधाय तु फलं दम्भार्थमपि चैव यत्।
इज्यते भरतश्रेष्ठ तं यज्ञं विद्धि राजसम् ॥
tr: abhisaṃdhāya tu phalaṃ dambhārthamapi caiva yat
ijyate bharataśreṣṭha taṃ yajñaṃ viddhi rājasam
en: But the sacrifice performed with an eye on its reward, or for show, know that to be of passion, best of the Bharatas.
The sacrifice that ignores scripture, shares no food, has no mantras, no gifts to the priests and no faith, is called one of dullness.
Reverence for the gods, the twice-born, teachers and the wise; purity, uprightness, celibacy and non-violence: this is called austerity of the body.

sa: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत्।
tr: anudvegakaraṃ vākyaṃ satyaṃ priyahitaṃ ca yat
en: Speech that causes no distress, that is truthful, pleasant and beneficial, and the regular study of sacred texts: this is called austerity of speech.
Serenity of mind, gentleness, silence, self-control and purity of heart: this is called austerity of the mind.
This threefold austerity, practised with supreme faith by disciplined people who seek no reward, is said to be of goodness.
Austerity practised to gain respect, honour and reverence, or for show, is said to be of passion; it is unstable and fleeting.
Austerity practised out of foolish obstinacy, by tormenting oneself, or to harm another, is said to be of dullness.

sa: देशे काले च पात्रे च तद्दानं सात्त्विकं स्मृतम् ॥
tr: deśe kāle ca pātre ca taddānaṃ sāttvikaṃ smṛtam
en: A gift given because it ought to be given, to one who can give nothing in return, at the right place and time and to a worthy person, is held to be of goodness.

sa: दीयते च परिक्लिष्टं तद्दानं राजसं स्मृतम् ॥
tr: dīyate ca parikliṣṭaṃ taddānaṃ rājasaṃ smṛtam
en: A gift given grudgingly, expecting something in return or with an eye on the reward, is held to be of passion.
A gift given at the wrong place and time to the unworthy, without respect or with contempt, is said to be of dullness.
"Om Tat Sat": this is said to be the threefold name of Brahman. By it, of old, the brahmins, the Vedas and the sacrifices were ordained.
So those who follow Brahman always begin the acts of sacrifice, giving and austerity taught by scripture by uttering "Om".
Uttering "Tat", seekers of freedom perform the various acts of sacrifice, austerity and giving without aiming at reward.

sa: प्रशस्ते कर्मणि तथा सच्छब्दः पार्थ युज्यते ॥
tr: praśaste karmaṇi tathā sacchabdaḥ pārtha yujyate
en: "Sat" is used in the sense of reality and of goodness; and the word "Sat" is also used for a praiseworthy act, Partha.

sa: यज्ञे तपसि दाने च स्थितिः सदिति चोच्यते।
tr: yajñe tapasi dāne ca sthitiḥ saditi cocyate
en: Steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity and giving is also called "Sat", and so is any action done for that purpose.

sa: अश्रद्धया हुतं दत्तं तपस्तप्तं कृतं च यत्।
असदित्युच्यते पार्थ न च तत्प्रेत्य नो इह ॥
tr: aśraddhayā hutaṃ dattaṃ tapastaptaṃ kṛtaṃ ca yat
asadityucyate pārtha na ca tatpretya no iha
en: Whatever is offered, given or practised as austerity without faith is called "asat", Partha; it is of no use here or hereafter.
